objective: Invite specific feedback on a free L/N pronunciation drill through one authentic first-party story, without implying clinical accuracy or customer outcomes.

supported_capabilities: Hear an L/N contrast and record one word
Inspect explainable practice feedback rather than a bare score
Switch practice among English, Mandarin, and Cantonese
Use the public browser version without creating an account
Follow a free light/night lesson with project-owned audio, mouth-placement images, captions, and video

release_state.policy: The Google Play production listing is independently public. TestFlight remains a beta route, and no public Apple App Store listing has been verified. Store availability is not evidence of a download, retained learner, lead, or revenue.

owned_discovery.policy: This is an owned discovery link to the free no-signup PWA and public source, not evidence of a tester, lead, sale, or store release.

owned_lesson.content: A standalone four-step light/night drill with exact listening cues, mouth-placement guidance, downloadable prompts, a captioned demonstration, and a quiet path into the free PWA.
owned_lesson.policy: This is project-owned educational evidence, not a learner result, pronunciation benchmark, clinical assessment, lead, sale, or public app-store release.

audio_repair.pwa: The iPhone browser path now records one microphone stream, retains the waveform after Stop, and requires recognized text before showing or saving a score.
audio_repair.apple: iOS and embedded watchOS build 2 include the repair and are available through TestFlight; the same build is waiting for formal App Review.
audio_repair.android: Android build 3 includes the no-empty-score repair plus release-only microphone permission and non-resolving Stop fixes. A signed release-emulator test showed the live waveform, a completed Stop flow, and no score for silence.
audio_repair.claim_boundary: Describe scores as explainable coaching feedback, never as clinical assessment or guaranteed pronunciation accuracy.

android_test_build.policy: Use only for an explicit tester invitation after rechecking the exact artifact and tester access; it is not evidence of public Google Play availability.

public_store_fix.change: The public README now points ordinary Android readers to the production listing instead of the restricted internal-test route.
public_store_fix.policy: Preserve the internal-test URL in historical tester evidence. A public listing is distribution evidence, not a download, feedback event, lead, payment, or revenue.

media.content: First-party L-and-N screens, icon, and bundled synthetic light/night prompts in an English and Traditional Chinese vertical demonstration.
media.claim_boundary: The clip is a product demonstration, not a customer result, accuracy benchmark, medical assessment, or public-store availability claim.

observations.need: An adult learner asked for an app or course that accommodates the L-initial pronunciation used by their Hong Kong Cantonese-speaking family.
observations.decision: No new reply. The thread is two months old, already contains several complete explanations and multiple app or course recommendations, and the author acknowledged those answers. Another product link would add little value under the community's no-spam rule.

observations.need: A current learner asked whether colloquial n-to-l variation applies across Cantonese words.
observations.decision: No new reply. The question already has many specific dialect and register answers and does not ask for a practice tool; linking the app would be promotion rather than the smallest useful answer.

need_research.outcome: The research supports a real pronunciation-learning need and the separate first-party educational post below. It did not create a Reddit interaction, tester, lead, customer, or revenue event.

linkedin.content:
I have trouble pronouncing L and N, so I built the practice tool I wanted.

Hear a pair, see the mouth and airflow cue, record one word, and get feedback you can inspect. The same four-minute drill works in English, Mandarin, and Cantonese.

It’s free and open source, and runs in the browser without an account:
https://l-and-n.lazying.art/

If you try it, tell me whether the mouth view actually makes the difference clearer.
